title: Infusion pumps
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Device-neutral educational specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.

parameters.name: Programmed rate
parameters.explanation: The programmed rate represents the intended delivery setting; it must match the authorised order. It is not independent proof that the patient is receiving the intended treatment.

parameters.name: Volume infused
parameters.explanation: The pump's displayed infused volume is a device estimate. Check it against the prescribed plan, bag or syringe and documented balance, and assess the patient for unexpected delivery.

safety_concepts.text: Verify programming (dosage, rate, volume) at change of shift, when any change is made to the settings, when a new bag is hung and when new tubing is primed (FDA).
Label pump channels and tubing at the port of entry with the drug or fluid name if the pump does not display it (FDA).
Use the drug library where one exists and respond carefully to alerts rather than silencing them (FDA).
Use independent double-checks for high-risk medicines where facility policy requires them, and use appropriate clinical monitoring to identify unexpected drug delivery.

escalation_concepts.text: Assess the patient and urgently escalate unexplained alarms, a programming discrepancy or suspected over- or under-infusion. For an essential high-risk infusion, stay with and closely monitor the patient while trained help obtains safe alternative equipment; avoid unplanned treatment interruption or an unintended bolus.

sources.use: ISMP high-alert medication list (2024): reproduction needs permission

The operator's manual for the specific model and software version the unit uses (identify it by name and version; do not reproduce its screens or alarm tables)
gaps: Parameter explanations are written only where a source read says something about the parameter; the rest stay unexplained (needs_source).
Safety, monitoring and escalation statements are reused from the matching skill draft and carry that draft's evidence support, not clinical review.
Any manufacturer-specific behaviour is excluded until a named model and software version, and permission to use its documentation, are available.
